findings.where: Steps 5, 6 and 12 (bearing picture, ship, winch): angle wedge and cos label
findings.what: The bearing's wedge is drawn at the tail between the north axis and the arrow, but the dashed north part is drawn at the far end of the triangle, so the cos label lands on a side that does not touch the marked angle and the picture contradicts 'the side next to the angle takes the cosine' at the lesson's key moment; mark the equal angle at the tip where the north part meets the arrow, or draw the parts north-first in bearing mode so the north part runs up the north axis beside the wedge.

findings.where: Step 3 slider (0° to 90°) and step 12 winch puzzle
findings.what: Resolving is never shown past 90°, yet the closing puzzle uses a bearing of 120, where 120° is not an angle of the right triangle and 'next to the angle' no longer applies, and it needs cos 120° to come out negative; let step 3's slider run round to 360° with signed readouts, or add one sentence on step 5 that east is size × sin and north is size × cos for any bearing, with the calculator giving the signs.
'only the cos label jumps' (and 'only the cos label moves') is not quite true, because the sin label and the angle wedge move too; say 'only the angle and its labels move'.
'This pull sits 30° above east, so its bearing is 060' skips that east is 090, and the leading zero of a three-figure bearing is never explained; add 'East is 090, so 30° back towards north is 060.'

The swapped answer −25i + 43.3j points north-west, so sign reasoning alone rules it out and the puzzle does not test where cos goes; use 25i − 43.3j as the swap so all wrong picks except the sign one point south-east.

With '1 square is 5 N' and '1 square is 2 knots' and the corner of the triangle on a grid line, he can count the answer (2 squares, 3 squares) without using cos or sin; consider a scale or angle that does not land the corner on a grid line.
'each part stays shorter than the pull until it lies along an axis': 'it' can be read as the part; say 'until the pull lies along an axis', as the read version does.

The picture tips the flat grid back into a floor, so y changes from up the page to along the floor, but no sentence says so and the read-through loses it; add 'The flat grid tips back to become the floor.'
'With i and j, the unit vectors along the axes, we write a = 3i + 4j' carries a mid-sentence aside; split it: 'i and j are the unit vectors along the axes. So a = 3i + 4j.'

findings.where: Step 3 picture at a steep angle (360 px light, 68°)
findings.what: The angle label '68°' sits against the dashed up part, its degree sign touching the dashed line; nudge the label inside the wedge or clamp it clear of the up part.

The [^1] footnote appears twice on a plain definition, not on a rule or value he would look up, and 'the separate x, y and z values' names z before the third axis is met; drop one footnote and say 'x and y' there.
